tavily.text:
To install Optiland, use the command `pip install optiland` for the core package. For the core package with a GUI, use `pip install optiland[gui]`. If you need GPU-enabled PyTorch, first install Optiland, then install a CUDA build of PyTorch manually. For development setup, clone the repository, create a virtual environment, and install the project with its dev dependency group using `uv sync --group dev`. The sources do not provide specific versions of Python or Optiland required for certain operations.
To install Optiland, use `pip install optiland` for the core package or `pip install optiland[gui]` for the core plus GUI. The documentation can be built locally with `pip install -r docs/requirements.txt` and the environment can be set up using `pip install -e "." --group dev` or manually installing packages listed under `[dependency-groups].dev` in `pyproject.toml`. For the documentation, it is published automatically on every push to `master` by the `Docs` workflow.
To install Optiland, you can use pip to install the package from PyPI. The latest version available is optiland-0.6.0. To install it, use the command `pip install optiland`. After installing Optiland, it is recommended to install a CUDA build of PyTorch manually using `pip install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu118`. The sources also mention that Optiland uses NumPy for fast CPU calculations and PyTorch for GPU acceleration and automatic differentiation.
